Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 1–2:

(p-689) Surat al-Rum is Meccan, and it has sixty or fifty-nine verses, the difference concerning a few of them.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim.﴾ ﴿The Romans have been defeated.﴾ That is: Persia (Faris) has defeated the Romans.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 3:

﴿In the nearest part of the land﴾: that is, the nearest land of the Arabs, because the land known to the Arabs is their own land. The meaning is: they were defeated in the nearest part of the land of the Arabs to them, namely the outskirts of al-Sham (Syria). Or it is meant: "their land," with the lam (ال) standing in place of the possessive pronoun, so that the sense is: in the part of their land nearest to their enemy. ﴿And they﴾, that is, the Romans, ﴿after their defeat﴾, that is, after the defeat of them at the hands of Persia. It is also read with a sukun on the lam (غَلْبِهِمْ), so al-ghalab and al-ghalb are both verbal nouns (masdar), and the verbal noun has been construed with its object. ﴿will overcome﴾ Persia. There is no pause (waqf) at this point, because of its grammatical connection (ta'alluq) with what follows.

**﴿In a few years﴾** (bid'a sinin). This is the span between three and ten. It is said: "Persia and the Romans fought between Adhri'at and Busra. Persia defeated the Romans, and the king of Persia at that time was Kisra Abraviz. The news reached Makkah, and it grieved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers, because Persia (p-690) were Magians who had no scripture, whereas the Romans were People of the Book. The polytheists rejoiced and gloated, and they said: 'You and the Christians are People of the Book, while we and the Persians are unlettered. Our brothers have prevailed over your brothers, and we will surely prevail over you.' So this was revealed. Abu Bakr said to them: 'By Allah, the Romans will certainly prevail over the Persians after a few years.' Ubayy ibn Khalaf said to him: 'You are lying.' They then wagered on it, ten she-camels from each of them, and they set the term at three years. Abu Bakr informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said (ﷺ): 'Increase the stake and lengthen the term.' So they made it one hundred she-camels, with a term of nine years. Ubayy died from a wound inflicted by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Romans prevailed over the Persians on the day of Hudaybiyya, or on the day of Badr. Abu Bakr then took the stake from the descendants of Ubayy, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Give it away in charity.'"

This is a clear sign of the truth of his prophethood and that the Qur'an is from Allah, for it is a report of unseen knowledge. And this occurred before the prohibition of gambling (qimar, games of chance).

From Qatada, and from the position of Abu Hanifa and Muhammad (al-Shaybani), is that void contracts, such as a contract involving riba (usury) and others, are permissible in dar al-harb (the land of war) between Muslims and disbelievers. They both argued for the validity of this ruling from this story.

﴿To Allah belongs the command, before and after﴾: that is, before everything and after everything. Or: before they were defeated and when they are defeated, and after they were defeated and when they will prevail. It is as if it were said: before their being victorious, which is the time of their being defeated, and after their being defeated, which is the time of their being victorious. The meaning is that their being defeated at first and victorious at last is nothing but by the command of Allah and His decree. ﴿And such days We alternate among the people﴾ [Al 'Imran: 140]. ﴿And on that day﴾: the day when the Romans prevail over the Persians and what Allah promised of their victory comes to pass, ﴿the believers will rejoice﴾.

﴿By the victory of Allah﴾ and His granting dominance to those who possess a Scripture over those who possess no Scripture, and to the chagrin of those among the disbelievers of Makkah who gloated over them. It is also said that "the victory of Allah" is the manifestation of the truthfulness of the believers in what they reported to the polytheists concerning the Romans' victory. The "bi" (by) is connected to "yafrahu" (will rejoice), and one pauses at "Allah" (p-691), not at "the believers rejoice in the victory of Allah."

﴿He grants victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty﴾, the Overpowering over His enemies, ﴿the Merciful﴾, the Compassionate toward His friends.

(ʿAbd Allāh, the tafsir text:) "Waʿda Allāh" (the promise of God) is a emphatic infinitive (maṣdar muʾakkad), because His saying "wa-hum min baʿdi ghalabihim sa-yaghlibūn" (and they, after their defeat, will be victorious) is a promise from God to the believers. So His saying "waʿda Allāh" is in the position of "waʿada Allāh al-muʾminīna waʿdan" (God promised the believers a promise). "Lā yukhlifu Allāh waʿdahu" (God does not break His promise) refers to the victory of the Romans over Persia. "Wa-lākinna akthara al-nāsi lā yaʿlamūn" (but most people do not know) that.

Note on terms: maṣdar muʾakkad (emphatic infinitive, a verbal noun used to reinforce the meaning of the verb).

﴿They know﴾ [al-Rum: 6] is a *badal* (substitute, in grammar an appositive that replaces the preceding term) for ﴿they do not know﴾ [al-Rum: 6]. In this there is a clarification that there is no difference between the absence of knowledge, which is ignorance (*jahl*), and the presence of a knowledge that does not go beyond acquiring worldly gain. His saying ﴿an outward [aspect] of the worldly life﴾ indicates that the world has an outward aspect (*zahir*) and an inward aspect (*batin*). Its outward aspect is what the ignorant know: enjoyment of its adornments. Its inward aspect is that it is a passage (*majaz*) to the Hereafter, from which one provisions oneself for it through obedience and righteous deeds. The indefiniteness of *zahir* (outward aspect) indicates that they know only one outward aspect out of its many outward aspects. ﴿And they, of the Hereafter, they are heedless﴾. *Hum* (they) the second is a *mubtada'* (subject of a nominal sentence), *ghafilun* (heedless) is its predicate, and the whole clause is the predicate of the first *hum*. In this there is a clarification that they are the source (*ma'dan*) of heedlessness of the Hereafter and its seat (*maqarr*).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 8:

﴿Have they not reflected within themselves?﴾ It may be that (*fi anfusihim*) is a *zarf* (adverbial of place, i.e., a locative complement), as if it were said: "Or have they not established reflection within themselves?" That is, in their hearts, which are empty of thought. Reflection occurs only in the heart, but this is an added depiction of the state of those who reflect, like your saying, "Believe it in your heart." It may also be a *silah* (complement) of *tafakkur* (reflection), as in *tafakkara fi al-amr* ("he reflected upon the matter") and *ajala fihi fikrahu* ("he directed his thought to it"). Its meaning according to this reading: "Have they not reflected upon themselves, which are closer to them than other created things, and they know their states better than they know the states of anything else, so that they would contemplate what Allah has deposited in them, outwardly and inwardly, of the wondrous wisdom that indicates an ordering (of affairs) and not neglect; and that they must come to an end at a time when they will be recompensed for good with good and for evil with its like, so that they would know at that time that all other creatures likewise have their affair proceeding according to wisdom in governance, and that they must come to an end at that time?"

﴿Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾ is connected to the omitted verb of saying. Its meaning: "Have they not reflected so that they would say this statement?" It was also said that its meaning is: (p-692) "so that they would know," because the speech contains an indication of it.

﴿except with truth and a specified term﴾ That is, He did not create them in vain and as play, without perfect wisdom, nor to remain eternal. Rather, He created them joined with truth, accompanied by wisdom, and with the appointing of a specified term to which they must come to an end, which is the establishment of the Hour, the time of reckoning, reward and punishment. Do you not see His saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115], how He named their not being returned to Him "vain."

﴿And indeed, many of the people are, in the meeting with their Lord﴾ — in the resurrection and the recompense — ﴿disbelievers﴾, that is, deniers. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 9:

﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ This is an affirmation of their journeying through the lands and their looking upon the traces of those who were destroyed, such as ʿAd and Thamud and others among the rebellious nations. Then he described their condition, saying: ﴿They were greater than them in strength and they stirred up the earth﴾ meaning they ploughed it and tilled it, ﴿and they cultivated it﴾ — that is, the ones who were destroyed — ﴿more than﴾ (akthar) is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun (maṣdar), and "mā" in ﴿more than what they cultivated﴾ is a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyyah), meaning: more than the cultivation of the people of Makkah. ﴿And their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾ — and one stops upon it (wa-taqifu ʿalayhā) because of the omission required (li-ḥaqq al-ḥadhf), meaning: so they did not believe and were destroyed. ﴿So Allah was not one to wrong them﴾ — so His destroying them was not an injustice to them. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾ — but they wronged themselves in that they did what necessitated their destruction.

ثُمَّ كانَ عاقِبَةَ — with the nasb (accusative) reading, transmitted by Shami and Kufi readers — ﴿the ending of those who did evil was the worst (al-suwa)﴾. The word al-suwa is the feminine of al-asw’a, meaning "the worst," just as al-husna is the feminine of al-ahsan ("the best"). Its position (mahall) is nominative (raf') if it is the ism of kana according to those who read ʿaqibatan as the khabar (predicate), and accusative (nasb) according to those who read it in the nominative.

The meaning is: they were punished in this world with destruction; then their ending was the worst (al-suwa), except that the apparent noun, namely "those who did evil," was placed in the position of the pronoun, meaning the punishment which is the worst of punishments in the Hereafter, which is the Fire prepared for the disbelievers ﴿because they denied﴾, because (p-693) they denied, or "that they denied." This indicates that the meaning of "did evil" is "disbelieved" ﴿in the signs of Allah, and they used to mock them﴾. That is: then the ending of the disbelievers was the Fire, because of their denial of the signs of Allah and their mockery of them.

﴿Allah originates the creation﴾, that is, brings them into being. ﴿Then He repeats it﴾, that is, gives them life after death. ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾. Abu 'Amr and Sahl read it with *bil-yā'* (بِالياءِ), meaning the verb is pronounced with a yā' prefix, *yur'jaʿūn* (يُرْجَعُونَ), in the third person, rather than with a tā' prefix.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 12:

﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will be in despair﴾ — yay'asu (they will despair) and yatahayyaru (they will be bewildered). It is said: "I debated with him, and he became silent (ablasa)," meaning when he did not utter a word and despaired of being able to argue. ﴿The criminals﴾ — the polytheists (al-mushrikun).

I need to translate this passage faithfully, following the rules: keep Qur'anic quotations in ﴿ ﴾ with plain meaning, transliterate technical terms with glosses on first occurrence, and keep Arabic script for discussed words in grammar notes.

﴿And there will be none for them among their partners﴾ — [those] whom they worshipped "besides Allah." It was written شُفَعَؤُا (shufa'a') in the muṣḥaf with a wāw before the alif, just as عُلَمَؤُا (ʿulamaʾu) of the Children of Israel was written, and likewise السُوأى (al-sū'a) was written with an alif before the yā', to indicate the hamza in the form of the letter from which its vowel-sign derives. ﴿And they will disbelieve in their partners﴾ — meaning: they will deny their gods and reject them; or, [it means] and they were, in the world, disbelievers because of them.

**﴿And on the day the Hour is established, on that day they will be divided.﴾** The pronoun in *yatafarraquna* ("they will be divided") refers to both the Muslims and the disbelievers, as indicated by what follows it, where He says:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 15:

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow﴾ That is, a garden, and it is Paradise. The indefiniteness (al-tankir) is for the vagueness of its matter and to magnify it. ﴿Where they will be made joyful﴾ That is, they will be gladdened. It is said: ḥabarahu (he made him joyful), when he gladdens him with a gladness that makes his face brighten and its trace appear upon it. Then it has been disputed concerning it, because of the many possible meanings of delight. It was said: they will be honored. It was said: they will be adorned. And it was said: it is listening (to music) in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 16:

﴿But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾ — i.e., the resurrection (al-ba'th) — ﴿they will be in the punishment, brought forward (muhdarun)﴾ — remaining (muqimun), not absent from it, and it will not be lightened for them, like His saying ﴿and they will not be removed from it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 37].

When He mentioned the promise and the threat, He followed it with a mention of what leads to the promise and saves from the threat, so He said: ﴿So glory be to God﴾. By glorification (al-tasbih) is meant its apparent sense, which is declaring God free of all imperfection and praising Him with good at these times, because of the manifest blessings of God that renew themselves in them. Or it means prayer (al-salat). It is related that Ibn 'Abbas was asked, "Do you find the five prayers in the Qur'an?" He said, "Yes," and recited this verse. The word (subhana) is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), and the meaning is: "Declare Him free of what is not fitting," or "Pray to God." ﴿When you enter the evening﴾ refers to the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾ refers to the Fajr prayer.

**[Commentary of al-Nasafi, *Madarik al-Tanzil*, on Surah 30, verse 18]**

﴿And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth﴾ is an *i'tiraḍ* (a parenthetical clause inserted within the discourse). Its meaning is that all discerning beings among the people of the heavens and the earth are obligated to praise Him. *Fi al-samawāt* (in the heavens) is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial qualifier) of *al-ḥamd* (praise).

﴿And in the evening﴾ refers to the prayer of *ʿaṣr* (the afternoon prayer). It is *maʿṭūf* (conjoined) to ﴿when you enter the evening﴾ [al-Rūm: 17].

﴿And when you enter midday﴾ refers to the prayer of *ẓuhr* (the midday prayer). *Aẓhara* means he entered the time of *ẓuhr* (midday).

The more widely held view is that the five daily prayers were enjoined in Mecca.

He brings the living out of the dead: the bird out of the egg, or the human out of the drop (nutfah), or the believer out of the disbeliever. ﴿And He brings the dead out of the living﴾: that is, the egg out of the bird, or the drop out of the human, or the disbeliever out of the believer. "Wa-l-mayyita" (وَالمَيْتَ), with the lightened pronunciation in both places, is read by Makki, al-Shami, Abu 'Amr, Abu Bakr and Hammad. The others read it with the doubled letter (tashdid). ﴿And He revives the earth﴾ with vegetation ﴿after its death﴾, its dryness. ﴿And thus you will be brought out﴾: tukhrajun (تُخْرَجُونَ) is read by Hamzah, Ali and Khalaf as "yukhrajun" in another form. That is, like this bringing forth, you will be brought out of your graves. The kaf (ك) in "wa-kadhalika" is in the place of nasb (accusative), governed by "tukhrajun". The meaning is that the origination and the return are equal in the power of the One who is able to bring the dead out of the living and the reverse.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ [al-Rum: 17] up to the three verses, and the end of Surat al-Saffat, after every prayer, there will be written for him good deeds equal to the number of the stars of the sky, the drops of rain, the leaves of the trees and the dust of the earth. And when he dies, there will be done for him, for every letter, ten good deeds in his grave."

And from him (ﷺ) he said: "Whoever recites in the morning ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ [al-Rum: 17] up to His saying ﴿And thus you will be brought out﴾, he will attain what he missed in his day. And whoever says it in the evening, he will attain what he missed in his night."

﴿And among His signs﴾ — that is, among the signs of His lordship and His power — ﴿is that He created you﴾ — i.e., your father — ﴿from dust; then, behold, you are human beings﴾ — i.e., Adam and his offspring — ﴿dispersing﴾ — spreading out, going about in what your livelihood lies in. Here "idha" (إذا, "behold") denotes suddenness (lil-mufaja'a), and its implied sense is: "then suddenly you were, at the time of your being human beings, dispersing over the earth."

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 21:**

﴿And among His signs is that He created for you, from yourselves, spouses that you may find tranquility in them﴾. That is: Hawwa' (Eve) was created from a rib of Adam, peace be upon him, and women after her were created from the loins of men. Or [they were created] from the likeness of your selves and their kind, not from a different kind. This is because of the familiarity and tranquility that exist between two of one kind, and because of the aversion that exists between two different kinds. It is said: "He found tranquility in him (sakana ilayhi)" when he inclined toward him. ﴿And He placed between you affection and mercy﴾. That is: He placed between you mutual affection and compassion through marriage. It is related from al-Hasan: "Affection is a metaphor for intercourse, and mercy is a metaphor for offspring." It is also said: "Affection is for the young woman and mercy is for the old woman." And it is said: "Affection and mercy are from Allah, and al-fark (mutual aversion) is from Satan," that is, the wife's hatred of her husband and the husband's hatred of his wife. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾, so that they know that the stability of the world depends on the existence of procreation. (p-696)

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 22:**

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your tongues﴾, meaning the languages, or the kinds and forms of speech, ﴿and your colours﴾, such as black and white and other than them. Because of this difference, recognition (al-ta'aruf) takes place. Otherwise, if they were alike and in agreement, there would be confusion and mutual indistinguishability, and the interests would be disrupted. In this is a clear sign, since they were born of one father, yet, in the great number known only to God, they differ from one another. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who know﴾. The word is the plural of ʿālam (world), and with a kasra on the lām, Ḥafṣ reads it as the plural of ʿālim (knower). The reading with the kasra is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And none understands them except those who know﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 43].

This is a commentary passage on Qur'an 30:23. Translating:

This is from the figure of speech called al-laff (interweaving, where two or more items are mentioned together and each is matched with a counterpart left implicit). Its original order is: "And among His signs is your sleep and your seeking of His bounty, by night and by day." However, it has separated the first two correlates by the other two correlates. Or the meaning is: your sleep at both times, and your seeking of His bounty in both of them. Most scholars hold the first view, because it recurs in the Qur'an, and the soundest of meanings is that which the Qur'an itself indicates.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who hear﴾, meaning: who hear with the hearing of reflection, with attentive ears.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 24:

﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning﴾. Regarding "yurīkum" (He shows you) there are two possibilities: the implicit insertion of "an" (that), as in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), and the placing of the verb in the position of a verbal noun (maṣdar). By these two possibilities the proverb "Hearing about the Mu'aydi is better than seeing him" has been explained, meaning: "that you hear" or "your hearing" (of him). ﴿With fear﴾ of the thunderbolt or of failure (of the rain), ﴿and hope﴾ for the rain, or fear for the traveller and hope for the one who stays at home. Both are in the accusative as objects of purpose (maf'ul lahu), with the omitted genitive noun (al-mudaf ilayhi) replaced by its position, meaning: "desiring fear" and "desiring hope"; or they are in the accusative of circumstance (hal), meaning: "fearing" and "hoping." ﴿And He sends down from the sky﴾ (the reading with the lightened form is that of Makki and Basri) (p. 697) ﴿water﴾, meaning rain, ﴿and gives life thereby to the earth after its death. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use their reason﴾, meaning who reflect with their minds.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 30, verse 25:

﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand firm by His command﴾ — they stand without pillars. ﴿by His command﴾ means: by His establishing them, His management, and His wisdom. ﴿Then, when He calls you﴾ to resurrection, ﴿with one call from the earth, behold, you will come forth﴾ from your graves. This is like His saying ﴿He shows you﴾ [al-Rum: 24], in placing the clause (*jumla*) in the position of a single noun (*mufrad*) according to meaning. It is as if He said: "And among His signs is the standing of the heavens and the earth and their holding firm without pillars, then the emergence of the dead from the graves when He calls them with one call: 'O people of the graves, come out!'" The intention is the swiftness with which that occurs, without any delay. He joined this to the standing of the heavens and the earth with *thumma* ("then") to clarify the magnitude of that matter and His power over the like of it, which is that He says, "O people of the graves, arise!" and not a single soul of the first and the last generations remains except that it stands up, looking on, as He said: ﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾ [al-Zumar: 68].

*Idha* (إذا) in the first position is conditional (*li-l-shart*), and the second *idha* is for suddenness (*li-l-mufaja'a*); it takes the place of the *fa'* (the particle of consequence) in the response of the condition. *Min al-ard* (مِنَ الأرْضِ, "from the earth") is connected to the verb, not to the verbal noun (*masdar*). Your saying "I called him from such-and-such a place" may mean that the place is your place, and it may mean the place of your companion.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 26:**

﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are obedient to Him﴾: submissive to the existence of His acts in them; they do not resist Him, or they acknowledge servitude (ʿubudiyyah) to Him.

He is the One who originates creation, ﴿and He is the One who began creation﴾, i.e., brings them into being, ﴿then repeats it﴾ for the resurrection, ﴿and that is easier for Him﴾, i.e., the resurrection, ﴿easier﴾, ﴿for Him﴾ according to you, because repetition is easier for you than initial creation, so why do you deny repetition? The complement (al-silah, the prepositional phrase that completes the predicate) is placed after the word in His saying ﴿and that is easier for Him﴾, but placed before it in His saying ﴿it is easy for Me﴾ [Maryam: 9], for the purpose of specification (al-ikhtisas, restricting the meaning to a particular party). Here, however, there is no sense in specification. Abu 'Ubayda, al-Zajjaj and others said: al-ahwan (the easier) has the meaning of al-hayyin (the easy), so it may be applied to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that was easy for Allah, as they say "Allah is the Greatest" meaning "Great." Repetition in itself is great, but it has been made easy by comparison with initial creation. Or it means: it is easier for the creatures than initial creation, because their being raised by a single cry is easier than their being sperm-drops, then clots, then lumps of flesh, until their creation is completed. ﴿And to Him belongs the highest likeness in the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., the highest attribute, which belongs to no one else, by which He is known and described in the heavens and the earth, on the tongues of creatures and on the tongues of the signs. It is that He is the Able, who is not incapable of anything, whether origination, repetition, or any other of the things that can be done. This is indicated by His saying ﴿and He is the Mighty﴾, i.e., the Subduer of every thing that can be done, ﴿the Wise﴾, who makes every act proceed in accordance with the dictates of His wisdom and knowledge. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that "the highest likeness" means ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾, and He is ﴿the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾. It is related from Mujahid that it is the saying "There is no god but Allah," and its meaning: to Him belongs the highest attribute, which is the attribute of oneness. His saying supports it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 28:

﴿He has coined for you a parable from yourselves.﴾ This is a parable that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has coined for the one who sets up a partner for Him from among His creation. The "min" (مِن) here denotes the starting point (li-l-ibtida'), as if He said: He took a parable and drew it from the closest thing to you, which is yourselves. ﴿Do you have﴾ — O free men — ﴿of what your right hands possess﴾ [al-Nur: 33] — your slaves — ﴿any partners﴾ — here "min" (مِن) is for partial reference (li-l-tab'id) — ﴿in what We have provided you with﴾ of wealth and other things? ﴿So you are﴾ — O free men and slaves — ﴿in it﴾ — in that provision — ﴿equal﴾ without any distinction between free man and slave, [such that] your slaves would have the same ruling over your wealth as you do. ﴿You fear them﴾ — a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun of the agent in "sawa'" (equal), meaning: you are equal, with some of you fearing others sharing with him in the wealth. The meaning is: O masters, do you fear your slaves in it, so that you do not carry out any ruling concerning it without their permission, out of fear of blame that would fall upon you from their side? ﴿As you fear one another yourselves﴾ — meaning: just as some free men fear one another in what is held in common between them. So if you are not pleased with this for yourselves, how can you be pleased for the Lord of lords, the Owner of free men and slaves, that you make some of His slaves partners to Him?! ﴿Thus﴾ — the place of the "ka" (كَ) is in the accusative — that is, like this detailed explanation, ﴿We detail the signs﴾ — We clarify them, because parables are among the things that reveal and make meanings clear. ﴿For a people who reason﴾ — who reflect upon the striking of parables. Then, when they did not heed, He turned away from them and said.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 29:

﴿Nay, those who did wrong followed their own desires﴾ (ﷺ not applicable) ... 

Let me restate the translation correctly:

﴿Nay, those who did wrong followed their own desires﴾ themselves, by associating partners [with Allah], as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13] ﴿their desires, without knowledge﴾, i.e., they followed their desires while ignorant. ﴿So who can guide one whom Allah has sent astray?﴾ i.e., whom Allah has sent astray, ﴿and they will have no helpers﴾ from the punishment.

﴿So set your face toward the religion﴾: straighten your face toward it, return to it, and do not turn aside from it to the right or to the left. This is an image of his turning toward the religion, his steadfastness in it, and his concern with its means. Whoever is concerned with something fixes his gaze on it, directs his look at it, and straightens his face toward it.

﴿hanifan﴾ (upright, inclining away from falsehood toward truth) is a state (ḥāl) either of the one addressed or of the religion.

﴿The fitra (natural disposition) of God﴾: adhere to the fitra of God. Fitra means creation or innate nature. Do you not see His saying, ﴿There is no alteration in the creation of God﴾? The meaning is that He created them disposed to accept monotheism (tawhid) and Islam, neither averse to it nor rejecting it, because it responds to reason and accords with sound reflection, so that if they were left alone they would not choose any other religion over it. Whoever among them went astray did so through the seduction of the devils of the jinn and of mankind. From this is his (ﷺ) saying: "Every one of My servants I created as ḥunafā'. Then the devils lured them away from their religion and commanded them to associate others with Me." And his (ﷺ) saying: "Every child is born upon the fitra, until his parents make him a Jew or a Christian."

Al-Zajjaj (d. 311 AH) said its meaning is that God the Exalted created the creation (p-٧٠٠) upon belief in Him, as in the hadith: "God the Mighty and Majestic brought forth from the loins of Adam his offspring like atoms, and made them bear witness against themselves that He is their Creator, and He said, ﴿And when your Lord took...﴾ [7:172] up to His saying ﴿They said, 'Yes'﴾ [7:172]." Every child is of that offspring who testified that God the Exalted is their Creator. So the meaning of ﴿the fitra of God﴾ is the religion of God ﴿upon which He created mankind﴾, that is, upon which He created them. ﴿There is no alteration in the creation of God﴾, that is, it is not fitting that that fitra be changed or altered. Al-Zajjaj said its meaning is: there is no alteration of the religion of God, and what follows supports this, namely His saying ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, that is, the straight one. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ the reality of that.

Turning back to Him in repentance (munībīna ilayhi): returning to Him. It is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to the pronoun in "ilzamū" (adhere to). The statement "wa-ittaqūhu" (and fear Him), "wa-aqīmū" (and establish), and "wa-takūnū" (and be) are conjoined (ma'ṭūf) to this implied pronoun, or to His saying "fa-aqim wajhaka" (so set your face). For the command addressed to him ﷺ is also a command to his community (ummah), so it is as if He said: "So set your faces (wujūhakum) upright, turning back to Him in repentance." Alternatively, the implied construction is "kūnū munībīna" (be those who turn back in repentance). Its evidence is His saying: ﴿And do not be﴾ [among those who fear Him], ﴿establish the prayer﴾ [Al-An'am: 72], meaning: perform it at its appointed times. ﴿And do not be among the polytheists﴾, those who associate others with Him in worship.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 32:

﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ [min alladhina, "of those who"] is a substitute (badal) for "al-mushrikin" (the polytheists), with the preposition repeated (bi-i'adat al-jarr).

﴿فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ﴾ ["they divided their religion"]: they made it into multiple religions, according to the differences of their desires (ahwa'ihim).

"Faraqu" (they parted from) is recited by Hamza and ʿAli, and it is the reading of ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him. That is: they abandoned the religion of Islam.

﴿وَكانُوا شِيَعًا﴾ ["and they became sects"]: groups, each one following (tushayi'u) its imam who misled it.

﴿كُلُّ حِزْبٍ﴾ ["every faction"] of them ﴿بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾ ["rejoicing in what they have"]: rejoicing in their own school of thought, pleased, thinking their falsehood to be truth.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 33:

﴿And when harm touches people﴾, a hardship of emaciation, or sickness, or drought, or other than that, ﴿they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him﴾, meaning, deliverance from the hardship, ﴿behold, a group of them associate others with their Lord﴾ in worship.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 34:

﴿So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them.﴾ This is the lam of purpose (lam kay). It has also been said that it is the lam of command, used for threat. ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ [Enjoy] for a little while: a command of threat. ﴿You will soon know﴾ the evil consequence of your enjoyment.

Surah 30, verse 35:

﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority﴾ (sultan), meaning a proof, ﴿so that it speaks﴾, and this speaking is figurative, as when you say "his book speaks of such-and-such," and what the Qur'an says is of this kind. Its meaning is testimony, as if He said: it bears witness to their polytheism and to its soundness, ﴿of what they have been associating with Him﴾. The word "ma" here may be a verbal particle (masdariyyah), meaning: by their associating others with Allah; or it may be a relative pronoun (mawsulah), with the pronoun referring back to it, meaning: it speaks of the matter because of which they associate partners. Or the meaning of the verse is: Or have We sent down to them one possessing authority, that is, an angel with whom is a proof, so that angel speaks of the proof because of which they associate partners.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 36:**

﴿And when We let mankind taste mercy﴾, that is, a blessing of rain, or abundance, or health, ﴿they rejoice in it﴾, they become insolent (baṭira) because of it, ﴿but when an evil befalls them﴾, that is, a calamity of drought, or hardship, or sickness, ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾, because of the ill effect of their sins, ﴿behold, they despair﴾ of mercy. Idhā (ﬁ) for suddenness is the answer of the conditional clause, standing in place of the fa', because the two share the sense of immediate sequence (ta'qib).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 37:

﴿Have they not seen that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ He rebuked them, because they already knew that He is the One who withholds and extends (al-qabid al-basit), so why do they despair of His mercy, and why do they not turn back to Him in repentance from the sins for which they were punished with hardship, until He restores His mercy to them?

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 38:

When he had mentioned that the evil had befallen them because of what their hands had earned, he followed it with mention of what must be done and what must be avoided. So he said: ﴿So give to the near of kin his due﴾, that is, give your relative his right of kindness and maintaining ties, ﴿and to the needy and the wayfarer﴾, their share of the charity (sadaqah) designated for them. In this is evidence that maintenance (nafaqah) is obligatory for the mahram relatives, as is our school's position. ﴿That﴾, i.e., giving them their rights, ﴿is better for those who desire the Face of Allah﴾, i.e., His Essence; that is, those who by their kindness intend Him alone sincerely. ﴿And those are the ones who will be successful.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 39:

﴿And whatever you give in riba (usury, excess gain) so that it may increase within people's wealth﴾ means: whatever you give to those who consume riba, so that it increases their wealth. ﴿It does not increase with Allah﴾, meaning it does not grow (yazku) with Allah and is not blessed. It is said that this refers to permissible riba (al-riba al-halal), that is, the gift you give so that you receive more than it in return. ﴿It does not increase with Allah﴾ because you did not intend by it the Face of Allah. ﴿And whatever you give in zakat﴾, that is, charity, ﴿seeking the Face of Allah﴾, meaning you seek by it His Face, sincerely, not seeking any recompense or showing off and seeking reputation. ﴿Those are the ones who multiply (al-mud'ifun)﴾, meaning those who have multiplied good deeds (dhawu al-id'af min al-hasanat). The counterpart of al-mud'if is al-muqwi (the one who is strong), and al-musir (the one who is wealthy) corresponds to dhu al-quwwa wa al-yasar (the one possessing strength and affluence).

"Ataytum min riba" is read without the Makkan mad (elongation), meaning: whatever you have brought, by giving riba. "Liturbu" is read by the Madinan reading, meaning: so that you may increase their wealth.

His saying ﴿Those are the ones who multiply﴾ is a fine shift (iltifat) in address, because it conveys generality, as if it were said: whoever does this, his path is the path of those addressed. The meaning is: those who are multiplied by it, because a relative pronoun (ma al-mawsulah) necessarily requires a pronoun referring back to it.

Al-Zajjaj said regarding His words ﴿fa-ulaʾika hum al-mud'ifun﴾: that is, its people are the multipliers, meaning they are those for whom the reward is multiplied; they are given ten times the like for each good deed. Then He pointed out the powerlessness of their gods, and said.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 40:

﴿Allah is He who created you﴾ [al-Rum: 40] is a mubtada' (subject) and khabar (predicate). ﴿Then He provided for you, then He will cause you to die, then He will give you life﴾ means: He alone is the one specific to creating, providing sustenance, causing death, and giving life. ﴿Is there any of your partners﴾ means: your idols, which you claimed were partners to Allah. ﴿who does any of that﴾ means: any of the creating, providing sustenance, causing death, and giving life. ﴿of anything?﴾ means: any single one of those acts. They did not answer, out of incapacity, so He said, in disbelief at them: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate.﴾ The first, second and third "min" (any) are each independent, serving as emphasis to show the incapacity of their partners and the ignorance of those who worship them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 41:

﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾, such as drought, scarcity of rain, a lack of yield in crops, a lack of profit in trade, the occurrence of pestilence (al-mawatan) among people and animals, the abundance of burning and drowning, and the erasure of blessings from everything. ﴿Because of what the hands of people have earned﴾, that is, because of their sins and their polytheism, like His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned﴾ [al-Shura: 30]. ﴿So that He may let them taste some of what they have done﴾, meaning: so that He may make them taste the consequence of some of their deeds in this world, before He punishes them for all of them in the Hereafter. It is read with the nun according to Qunbul: ﴿so that they may return﴾, from what they are upon of sins. Then he emphasized that sins are the cause of the wrath of God and His punishment by His saying.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 42:

﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and see what was the end of those before you; most of them were polytheists."﴾ Here He commanded them to travel and look, to see how Allah destroyed the nations and made them taste the evil end of their disobedience.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 43:

﴿So set your face toward the upright religion﴾ (al-Din al-Qayyim), the one that is perfect in uprightness, in which no crookedness can be found. ﴿Before there comes a Day which cannot be turned back﴾ (maradd). It is a verbal noun meaning "return" (radd). ﴿From Allah﴾ relates to "yati" (comes), and the meaning is: before there comes from Allah a Day which no one can turn back, like His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿So they will not be able to repel it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 40]. Or it relates to "maradd," in the sense that no one can turn it back once it has come, and there is no repelling of it on His part. ﴿On that Day they will be separated﴾ (yasadda'un), i.e., they will be scattered (yatafarraqun). (p-704)

Then he pointed to His sufficiency, saying: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾, i.e., the burden of his disbelief. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare [the way]﴾, i.e., they make ready for themselves what one makes ready for his own self, one who spreads out his bed for himself and smooths it, lest there befall him in his resting-place anything that disturbs his sleep, such as a bump or other thing. The meaning is: He prepares for them the Garden because of their deeds, so it is attributed to them. The placing of the prepositional phrase first in both places indicates that the harm of disbelief returns only upon the disbeliever, while the benefit of faith and righteous deeds returns to the believer and does not go beyond him.

Translation:

﴿That He may reward﴾ is connected to "yamhudun" (they prepare the way for themselves), as its purpose, and it is a repetition of it. ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. The pronoun was left in favour of the explicit noun, to indicate that none is successful before Him except the believer. ﴿of His bounty﴾, that is, of His giving. And His saying ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers﴾ is a confirmation after a confirmation, by way of direct and reverse implication (al-tard wa al- 'aks).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 46:

﴿And among His signs﴾, i.e., among the signs of His power, ﴿is that He sends the winds﴾. They are the south wind (al-janub), the north wind (al-shamal), and the east wind (al-saba), and they are winds of mercy. As for the west wind (al-dabur), it is a wind of punishment. From this is his saying ﷺ: «O Allah, make them winds and do not make them a wind». He has enumerated the benefits of sending them, so He said: ﴿bearing good tidings﴾, i.e., He sends them to give the good tidings of rain. ﴿And that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾, and for letting one taste mercy, which is the descent of rain, the abundance of fertility that follows it, the refreshment that comes with the blowing of the wind, the purification of the land, and other things. Wa-liyudhiqakum is conjoined (ma'tuf) to mubashshirat in meaning: it is as if it were said, "so that He may give you good tidings and so that He may let you taste." ﴿And that the ships may sail﴾ on the sea when they blow, ﴿by His command﴾, i.e., by His ordinance (tadbir) or His bringing into being (takwin), as in His saying: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82], the verse. ﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning the trade of the sea. ﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾, and that you may thank Allah for His blessing therein. (p-705)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 47:

﴿And We certainly sent before you messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs﴾. That is: so some people believed in them, and some people disbelieved in them. What indicates this implied meaning is His saying ﴿So We took retribution from those who committed crime﴾, that is: who disbelieved, by destroying them in this world. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾, that is: and the help of the believers was incumbent upon Us, by saving them along with the messengers. It may be pause at "ḥaqqan" (incumbent), and its meaning would be: and the retribution against them was a truth; then you begin with ﴿upon Us is the help of the believers﴾. The first (reading) is more sound.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 48:

﴿Allah is He Who sends the winds﴾ al-Riyah (the winds), in the Meccan reading (Makki) with the singular al-Rih. ﴿So they stir up clouds, and He spreads them in the sky﴾ i.e., the clouds, ﴿in the sky﴾ i.e., in the direction and expanse of the sky, like His saying ﴿and its branches in the sky﴾ [Ibrahim: 24]. ﴿However He wills﴾ from the direction of the north, or the south, or the west (dabur), or the east (saba). ﴿And makes them into fragments﴾ qita'an (pieces), the plural of kisfa; i.e., He makes it spread out, taking the face of the sky at one time, and makes it into scattered pieces, not spread out, at another time. "Kisfan" is read by Yazid and Ibn Dhakwan. ﴿Then you see the rain﴾ al-wadq (the rain) ﴿coming out﴾ in both readings together, ﴿from within it﴾ from its midst. ﴿Then when He causes it to strike﴾ with the rain ﴿whom He wills of His servants﴾ meaning, He intends it to fall on their lands and their fields, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾ yafrahun (they are glad).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 49:

﴿And indeed they were, before it was sent down upon them﴾ the rain, ﴿before it﴾. [The phrase] is repeated for emphasis, like His saying ﴿So the end of both of them is that they will be in the Fire, abiding therein﴾ [al-Hashr: 17]. The meaning of emphasis here is the indication that their wait for the rain had lengthened, so their despair became firmly established, and therefore their joy at it was in proportion to their former distress over it. ﴿Despairing﴾, i.e., hopeless.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 50:

﴿Then look at the traces﴾ of Shami and Kufi readers other than Abu Bakr, and others read "athar" ﴿of the mercy of Allah﴾, meaning the rain, ﴿how He gives life to the earth﴾ with plants and various kinds of fruits ﴿after its death. Indeed, that﴾, meaning Allah, ﴿is the Giver of life to the dead﴾. The meaning is: that Capable One who gives life to the earth after its death is the One who gives life to people after their death. This is an argument from the revival of the dead earth to the revival of the dead ﴿and He is Able over all things﴾, meaning: He is Able over everything among the things that can be done, and this is among the things that can be done, as evidenced by the origination (of creation).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 51:

﴿And if We send a wind﴾, namely the west wind (al-Dabur), ﴿and they see it﴾, i.e., the effect of God's mercy, for God's mercy is the rain and its effect is vegetation. Whoever reads with the plural (ātharihi, "its effects") has the pronoun refer to its meaning, because the meaning of "effects of mercy" is vegetation, and the noun "vegetation" (nabat) applies to both the few and the many, since it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) by which that which grows is named. ﴿Yellowed﴾ after its greenness. He said "yellowed" (muṣfarran) because that yellowness is something newly arisen. It is also said: "they see the cloud yellowed," because a yellow cloud does not rain. The lam in ﴿la-in﴾ is a preparatory lam (lam al-muwaṭṭi'ah) for the oath, entering upon the conditional particle, and it serves in place of the answers of both the oath and the condition. ﴿Surely they would remain﴾, its meaning being "they would surely remain" (la-yaẓallunna), ﴿after it disbelieving﴾, i.e., after its yellowing, or after the rejoicing. God censures them: when He withholds rain from them, they despair of His mercy and strike their chins upon their chests, dejected (mublisīn). Then, when He reaches them with His mercy and provides them rain, they rejoice. And when He sends a wind that strikes their crops with blight (al-ṣifār), they cry out and disbelieve the blessing of God. So they are, in all these states, in the blameworthy attribute. It was incumbent upon them to rely upon God and His bounty, yet they despaired; and to be thankful for His blessing and praise Him for it, yet they rejoiced; and to be patient under His trial, yet they disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 52:

﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾: that is, the dead of heart; or these people are in the position of the dead, so do not hope that they will accept from you. ﴿Nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾, and the deaf do not hear (the reading of Makki, "ولا يَسْمَعُ الصُمُّ"). ﴿When they turn away, retreating﴾. If you say: the deaf person does not hear whether he is facing you or turned away, so what is the benefit of this specification? I say: when he is facing you, he understands through gesture and signs; but when he turns away, he neither hears nor understands by signs.

﴿Nor are you a guide for the blind﴾ [al-Naml: 81], i.e., the blind of heart. "Nor can you guide the blind" (Ḥamzah). ﴿from their error﴾, i.e., you cannot guide a blind man to a path he has strayed from by pointing him toward it. ﴿You can only make hear﴾ what you make hear ﴿those who believe in Our signs, and they are submissive﴾, compliant with the commands of God, Exalted is He. (p-707)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 54:

﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness﴾ from the drops of semen, like His saying ﴿from a despised water﴾ [al-Sajdah: 8]. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, meaning: the state of youth and reaching maturity (al-ashudd). ﴿Then He made after strength weakness and grey hair﴾, meaning: the state of old age and decrepitude. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾ of weakness, strength, youth and grey hair. ﴿And He is the All-Knowing﴾ of their conditions, ﴿the All-Powerful﴾ over changing them. This alternation of states is the clearest proof of the Creator who is All-Knowing and All-Powerful.

ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read the ḍād (ض) in all of them as a fatḥah (ضَعْفٍ, ḍaʿf), while others read it with a ḍammah (ḍuʿf), which is the choice of Ḥafṣ. Both are dialectal variants (lughatān), but the ḍammah is stronger in recitation because of what has been transmitted: "On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I recited it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as min ḍaʿf, and he taught me min ḍuʿf."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 55:

﴿And on the day the Hour (al-sa'a) is established﴾: i.e., the Resurrection (al-qiyama). It is so named because it is established at the last hour (sa'a) of the worldly life (al-dunya), or because it comes suddenly, as you say "in an hour" (fi sa'a) to someone whom you want to hurry. It has become a proper name for it, like the Pleiades (al-Thurayya) being named by the star (al-najm).

﴿The criminals will swear﴾: the disbelievers will take an oath. There is no pause (waqf) on this, because ﴿they remained﴾ in the graves, or in the world, ﴿for no more than an hour﴾ is the answer of the oath. They will consider the duration of their stay in the graves, or in the world, to be brief, due to the terror of the Day of Resurrection and the length of their stay amid its hardships. Or they will forget, or they will lie.

﴿Thus were they turned away﴾: i.e., in the same way as that turning away, they used to be turned away from truthfulness to falsehood in the world, and they used to say, "There is nothing but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."

"And those who were given knowledge and faith will say," — they are the prophets, the angels and the believers. ﴿You had indeed remained, by the Book of Allah,﴾ that is, by the knowledge of Allah recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh), or by the decree and judgment of Allah, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection.﴾ They refuted what the disbelievers had said, swore to it, and informed them of the reality. Then they linked this with a rebuke for their denial of resurrection, by saying: ﴿This is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not⁠ [knowing]⁠⁠ —⁠ "in the world" —⁠ "knowing" that it is true, because of your neglect in seeking the truth and following it.⁠ The fa' (then/so) is the response to a conditional (shart) implied by the speech, whose sense is: "If you were deniers of resurrection, then this is the Day of Resurrection that you denied."

**[Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 30, verse 57]**

﴿So on that Day no excuse will benefit those who did wrong﴾, read with the *yā'* (بِالياءِ) by the Kufan reader (one of the Kufan readers of the Qur'an). *Those who did wrong* means those who disbelieved. *Their excuse* means their pretext. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾. That is, it will not be said to them, "Please your Lord by repentance." It derives from your saying: *is'ta'tabanī fulān fa-a'tabtuhu*, meaning he asked me to be pleased with him, so I pleased him.

Qur'anic verse: "And We have certainly presented to people in this Qur'an every kind of example. And if you were to bring them a sign, those who disbelieve would surely say, 'You are nothing but falsifiers.'"

That is: We have certainly described to them every attribute that is strange as an example, and recounted to them every story of wondrous matter, such as the description of those raised up on the Day of Resurrection, their story, what they say, what is said to them, their excuses which do not benefit them, and their pleas for forgiveness which are not heeded. But because of the hardness of their hearts, when you bring them a sign from the signs of the Qur'an, they say, "You have brought us nothing but falsehood and lies."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 59:

﴿Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know.﴾ That is: like that sealing (ṭabʿ), which is the sealing-up (khatm), Allah seals the hearts of the ignorant (jahalah) whom Allah has known to choose misguidance, to the extent that they call the people of truth (al-muḥiqqīn) "falsifiers" (mubṭilīn), and they are the most deeply rooted of Allah's creatures in that attribute.

"So be patient" (against their harm or their enmity), "indeed the promise of Allah" of victory for you over your enemies and the manifestation of the religion of Islam over every religion "is true," there is no escape from its fulfilment and keeping it. "And let not those who have no certainty steer you to lightness" — that is: let not those who have no certainty of the Hereafter move you to lightness and haste in invoking punishment upon them, or let them not move you to lightness and agitation out of distress at what they say and do, for they are misguided doubters, and such conduct from them is not to be wondered at. The reading "wa-la yastakhiffannka" with the nun sukun is from Ya'qub (the transmitter of the reading), and Allah is the Granter of success to what is right.
